Authors:[Muyu He](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=He,+M), [Adit Jain](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Jain,+A), [Anand Kumar](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Kumar,+A), [Vincent Tu](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Tu,+V), [Soumyadeep Bakshi](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Bakshi,+S), [Sachin Patro](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Patro,+S), [Nazneen Rajani](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Rajani,+N)
View a PDF of the paper titled $\texttt{YC-Bench}$: Benchmarking AI Agents for Long-Term Planning and Consistent Execution, by Muyu He and 6 other authors
[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.01212v1) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.01212v1)
> Abstract:As LLM agents tackle increasingly complex tasks, a critical question is whether they can maintain strategic coherence over long horizons: planning under uncertainty, learning from delayed feedback, and adapting when early mistakes compound. We introduce \texttt{YC-Bench}$200K, with Claude Opus 4.6 achieving the highest average final funds at $1.27 M, followed by GLM-5 at $1.21 M at 11\times47\%\texttt{YC-Bench}
